📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that red, red, green — those are the party colors of the left-leaning coalition recently formed in the German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Now a Berlin-based agency wants to see the same alliance between the center-left Social Democrats, the socialist Left Party, and environmentalist Greens win the 2029 national elections.

Industry observers note that the Goodforces wants to help make that a reality with their campaign neunund20 (twenty-nine), taking its cue, in part, from the American left. The agency was set up in response to the rise of the far right across Europe.

Co-founder Patrick Haermeyer told DW that the campaign's aim is "to give people hope and an alternative narrative to: Things are getting worse and worse." He worked as an online organizer for the election team of Bernie Sanders in the US Democratic presidential primaries in 2016 and cites Sanders' "not me, us" campaign as an inspiration.

Neunund20 presently has two strategies: It provides digital space for short-form videos and social media content on political and social topics on Instagram, Tiktok, and Bluesky. At the same time, it tries to connect content creators, activists, NGOs, and political initiatives around shared "progressive" challenges.

Users with a particular interest can click to get a link giving them access to archives of relevant social media material that they can then reshare. That feature is modelled on the campaign of New York's left-wing mayor Zohran Mamdani.

And there are other projects. The Goodforces was recently involved in a tactical voting initiative in the September elections in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, intended to keep the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) from winning an absolute majority. Haermeyer indicates physical campaigns of that kind are necessary to provide essential "interim victories" en route to the next parliamentary elections.

It has been revealed that the Greens and the SPD, the two parties recommended by the app created by the organization, made it over the 5% hurdle and into parliament. The help that they received was declared by each party in the form of a €40,000 ($43,900) donation.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The agency sees itself as a kind of Super PAC, modeled on political organizations in the United States that collect money to carry out campaigns without directly supporting a single party or a special candidate.

For Christoph Bieber, political scientist at the University of Duisburg-Essen, the Goodforces is an interesting new type of player on Germany's political scene because it operates outside the country's political parties.

But many of those parties are eyeing the development with disquiet. The far-left, populist, immigration skeptical Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW) criticized the Goodforces' intervention in Saxony-Anhalt, telling the newspaper FAZ that it was an "infantilizing, and perhaps even antidemocratic action." The neoliberal Free Democrats (FDP) called the tool "wrong and intentionally misleading." The FDP failed to clear the threshold, while the BSW only just squeaked in. The AfD gained 43% of the vote and its candidate may soon become Germany's first far-right state premier since the Nazi era.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Haermeyer set up the agency in 2024 along with Peter Jelinek, and both men previously worked for Green Party European Parliament member Michael Bloss. Ahead of that year's European elections, the EU's Green Deal began to come under increasing attack.

That year also ended with the collapse of Germany's first federal coalition between the SPD, Greens, and FDP, after much infighting and attacks from right-wing quarters.

According to recent reports, "We noticed that more and more successes and freedoms that we had fought for were being reversed: Things like freedom of movement, border checks, and other things that were coming more and more under fire," Haermeyer told DW. "And we noticed that it was primarily democratic and progressive forces that were being drawn into defensive battles.".

The AfD, founded in 2013, already in the age of social media, has successfully targeted younger voters with in its online campaigns. But the older parties, in particular, have struggled. The Goodforces saw a need for support in the online environment and is now seeking to plug this gap.

The social media accounts of the campaign neunund20 contain posts on domestic German topics, such as the current negotiations to form a red-red-green coalition government in Berlin, and the country's new military service law. They also highlight "wins" in Spain in the protests for affordable housing and for US Democrats in the midterms.

Haermeyer stresses that the issues the agency highlights are determined together with a wide range of grassroots organizations and activists. "The campaign is not agreed in conjunction with the SPD, the Left Party, and the Greens," he said.

Sources indicate that agency funding comes from commissions and small donations. Haermeyer says that contributions generally range from $20 to $50.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Bieber sees the emergence of non-party campaigning, long an accepted practice in the US, as a bid to compensate for the shortcomings of traditional parties.

Industry observers note that "It is an omission of the parties," he noted. "For years they have been saying we have to modernize, we have to become more open and get away from rigid membership structures. There are legal regulations governing the organization of political parties in Germany, but perhaps it could be more flexible and open.".

In a recent development, the center-left and center-right significant-tent parties have been in decline for decades. Membership of the SPD dropped from 943,000 in 1990 to some 348,000 at the end of 2025. Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) has seen a fall from 750,000 to under 357,000.

In a recent development, party membership is particularly low in former communist eastern Germany. Centrist parties have also struggled to attract younger voters. A report by the Deutsche Kinder und Jugendstiftung (German Children and Youth Foundation) demonstrated that only 20% of young people felt their concerns were taken seriously in the 2025 German elections and that trust in parties was low.

In the United States, campaign financing comes predominantly from donations, and lobby groups can buy influence by contributing unlimited amounts to super PACs. In Germany, party funding comes, in part, from taxpayers and membership fees, and donations are capped. However, Bieber warns that whereas there are strict rules regarding the disclosure of donors to US Super PACs, these do not exist in Germany.

According to recent reports, the political scientist does not believe that US-style campaigning is going to take hold in Germany, but he does see potential dangers: "This could be a door opener to make others consider whether they want to go in this direction in the field of campaigning. And he added: "If it becomes rife, it could lead to a further devaluation of parties and their structures.".

Lincoln sack head coach duo Cohen and Shaw after only six months

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (745 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chris Cohen (left) and Tom Shaw had been on the coaching staff together at Lincoln for a number of years before they got the top job together.
  • Lincoln City have sacked their head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw just six months after they took joint charge of the Championship side.
  • The pair departed a little over 12 hours after they oversaw a 4-0 defeat at fellow strugglers Charlton Athletic on Tuesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chris Cohen (left) and Tom Shaw had been on the coaching staff together at Lincoln for a number of years before they got the top job together.

Lincoln City have sacked their head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw just six months after they took joint charge of the Championship side.

The pair departed a little over 12 hours after they oversaw a 4-0 defeat at fellow strugglers Charlton Athletic on Tuesday.

The loss leaves the Imps just three points above the relegation places in what is the club's first season back in the second tier for 65 years.

Cohen and Shaw were assistant coaches under Michael Skubala when Lincoln were promoted as League One title winners last season.

They were surprisingly promoted to replace their boss as a managerial double act.

Championship survival behind sackings - Imps CEO.

Charlton brush aside outclassed Lincoln.

What next for Lincoln City after coach duo exit?

The duo oversaw just four wins from 17 league games this season, and Tuesday's loss at The Valley was their fifth in succession and heaviest since being thumped 6-0 by West Ham in mid-October.

Lincoln's chairman Ron Fowler, the American billionaire who took a controlling stake in the club when they were on their way to promotion last season, said the decision to sack the pair was in the "best interests" of the Imps.

"We have worked incredibly hard to reach the Championship and will do everything in our power to retain our status in this division," he told the club website., external.

First-team coach Shaun Pearson will take charge of Lincoln, with the support of Paul McShane and David Preece, on an interim basis.

Lincoln are next in action on Saturday when they host high-flying Wolves.

When Cohen and Shaw got the job at Sincil Bank it came somewhat as a shock because managing football teams in tandem is somewhat of a curiosity in the game.

Liverpool famously did with Gerard Houllier and Roy Evans in 1998 when the partnership lasted six months as results slumped, while Tottenham gave it a go with Doug Livermore and Ray Clemence earlier that same decade.

The hope was that the Cohen-Shaw show would be a lot more like Coventry's success story under John Sillett and George Curtis, who guided the Sky Blues to FA Cup glory in 1987.

Lincoln's decision-makers were proactive in talking up their decision, with sporting director Jez George explaining in June that the appointment "wasn't a case of do the easy thing, but it was absolutely the right thing for the club".

Shaw and Cohen were also quizzed at length about how the joint role would work, starting with "who's going to make the subs?".

Cohen was upfront when he mentioned "from the outside looking in, it's not normal", but the former Nottingham Forest and West Ham midfielder insisted that the job share was "really normal" to them.

How peculiar it might have looked, or how the dynamics between the pair worked, all become somewhat irrelevant in recent weeks as Lincoln's dire run of form has plunged them towards the relegation places.

Follow Lincoln City on BBC Sounds.

Pre-match, post-match and topical Imps content.

BBC Radio Lincolnshire's Rob Makepeace.

Lincoln City fans always thought this season would be tough and that they'd lose more than they win, but it was the manner of the performances recently that was most concerning.

Strange team selections in the past two matches in particular, including playing left-back Adam Reach as a right winger against Charlton Athletic in their final match in charge, was always going to raise questions, especially when the results didn't go their way, and that has ultimately been the case.

The appointment of Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw was going to be seen as a risk - joint managers/head coaches very rarely work and add in the lack of managerial experience, especially at this level.

First-team coach Shaun Pearson, who only recently joined the club , now has the task to try to turn a team low on confidence, low on ideas and low on belief into one that can stop one of the promotion favourites in Wolves on Saturday lunchtime.

Whoever's next in the dugout, however, won't come in with a massive jump in expectations of a climb up the table.

Imps supporters will be more than happy to just see their side secure a second season in the Championship.

The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided.

Sign up for our free newsletter here.

In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter.

Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0. Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023. Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some things are certain in life; death, taxes and Watford sacking another head coach.

At 11:51am on Sunday morning, the news everyone expected had arrived and Alessio Dionisi was relieved of his duties as Watford head coach after five months in charge, following a dismal 4-0 away defeat to Sheffield United, which left the club just one place above the relegation zone.

It was the latest in a series of lifeless performances from a Watford side that have looked ill-equipped for Championship football from the moment the season started.

Now, at a time where Watford need Championship experience more than ever, owner Gino Pozzo has gone turned to former Romania boss Edward Iordanescu, a man that has had 13 jobs in 15 years, never managed more than 60 games at any team and most importantly, never played or coached in England or in one of Europe’s major leagues.

Given Watford’s reputation with head coaches, many would joke Iordanescu’s appointment sounds like a match made in heaven.

For Hornets fans, though, it’s an act of desperation from a club that has no proposal, structure or hope.

In truth, Dionisi is the latest in a series of head coaches who have been let down by owner Pozzo, chairman Scott Duxbury and technical director Gianluca Nani, who seem incapable of building a squad or supporting a head coach.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Industry observers note that things could have been so different for the Italian, because at the start of the season, there was clearly something there. Watford were excellent in their opening day win over Southampton - playing with real flair and intensity in the first half - and followed that up with draws against Wrexham and West Ham. It was clear the players respected the Italian.

In a recent development, however, the warning signs were already there. In the summer, Dionisi and supporters were told that Watford would prioritise experienced players in the transfer market. None arrived.

Nestory Irankunda, Imran Louza and Giorgi Chakvetadze - three key players - were sold and not replaced, with Watford starting the season with just two centre-backs on the club’s books and two fit central midfielders.

Sources indicate that the Italian sounded increasingly exasperated as his calls for reinforcements fell on deaf ears until the final few days of the window, where Watford eventually panicked and brought in Stephy Mavididi, Soumaila Coulibaly and Branimir Mlacic on loan. Myron Boadu and Michail Antonio arrived on free transfers.

According to recent reports, most of those players arrived unfit and come September, Dionisi was struggling to fill the bench as injuries took hold. The Italian never really recovered from embarrassing defeats to Burnley and Cardiff City, deploying a back five in recent weeks as he attempted to make the Golden Boys harder to beat.

In a recent development, quite frankly, Watford are unmanageable. Not even Pep Guardiola would be successful at Vicarage Road, because no head coach is given the opportunity to implement a style of play when they have to contend with poor recruitment, a leadership vacuum and a dressing room with seemingly poor attitudes.

According to recent reports, rob Edwards was promised he'd be backed in the transfer market come hell or high water by chairman Duxbury in the summer of 2022. Most of the signings he received didn't fit his system and he was sacked within two months of the season starting.

According to recent reports, after Edwards, Slaven Bilic thought he'd be able to sign players he wanted in the January transfer window. He received Joao Ferreira and Henrique Araujo - both of whom never looked suited to Championship football – as well as Ryan Porteous, Wesley Hoedt and Britt Assombalonga. Bilic was gone by March.

It has been revealed that then came Chris Wilder, who repeatedly called out the poor attitude within the dressing room and wasn't given a contract extension when his deal expired in the summer of 2023. After the wheels came off under Valerian Ismael, Tom Cleverley was promoted to head coach in 2024 and despite a thin squad, united the players and fans, having been a popular player at Vicarage Road during his playing days.

Once again, though, January arrived and Cleverley didn't get the options he so dearly needed, meaning Watford's form dropped off and he was sacked, somewhat harshly, at the end of the season.

Recent findings suggest that just last season, the popular Javi Gracia returned for a second spell in charge and had Watford in the play-off spots by January. He was promised additions, but none were forthcoming and ultimately the Spaniard decided the job wasn't worth his time. Gracia resigned, returning to Spain to spend time with his family.

Sources indicate that in short, it's time the Watford ownership took a long, hard at themselves, rather than the head coach. Has Iordanescu been appointed because no one sensible will take it? Any head coach worth his salt in England - and possibly now Italy, too - knows what they’re walking into.

In a recent interview with Roy Moore from the 1881 Movement, Pozzo tried shifting accountability for the club’s downfall, which can be traced back to the FA Cup Final in 2019. Since then, numerous decisions have, in the eyes of supporters, led to the erosion of the club's identity - fans have had enough.

Empty statements, the constant churn of players and head coaches, and what appears to be a lack of any real structure or strategy - supporters are fed up.

The fact Watford closed their Under-21 setup, downgraded their academy and sold off the women's team this summer was a huge source of disappointment for fans, too, given the club’s rich history of bringing players through their youth system.

Unless there is a sudden change of approach overnight, Watford are only heading one way and that's down to League 1.

#116722. Are Manchester United this season's Tottenham?

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Are Manchester United this season's Tottenham?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (845 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United are in the Premier League relegation zone 11 games into the season.
  • Last season, Tottenham - a member of the so-called 'substantial six' - escaped relegation from the Premier League on the final day.
  • Now, with Manchester United making their worst start to a league season since 1972, it raises the question: are United this season's Spurs?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United are in the Premier League relegation zone 11 games into the season.

Last season, Tottenham - a member of the so-called 'substantial six' - escaped relegation from the Premier League on the final day.

Now, with Manchester United making their worst start to a league season since 1972, it raises the question: are United this season's Spurs?

While Tottenham finished 17th with just 41 points last term, they actually started the season better than United have this season. After 11 games in 2025-26, Spurs were riding high in fifth with 18 points - 10 more than United have now.

But one of the biggest myths in football is 'the table never lies' and it was certainly lying about Tottenham at this stage last season.

While the table prompted talk of a possible Champions League place, expected goals (xG) had already recognised a relegation battle lay ahead for Tottenham, even predicting the position they'd finish in.

United's expected goal difference is almost identical to Tottenham's at this stage last season, but this time the table is more honest, even if United are perhaps not as bad as it makes out.

But there's no denying United's statistics are those of a team in a relegation battle, with many of them in the bottom six of Premier League teams this season.

While United have performed poorly defensively, their attack is actually not bad.

Remarkably, United have taken the most shots in the Premier League so far this season, and their expected goals scored figure is in the top five.

But what upcoming head coach Mauricio Pochettino has to implement rapidly is some quality control when it comes to shots at both ends of the pitch. United are converting just 7% of their chances and conceding 16% of their opponents' - a poor combination for any team.

And it is not simply down to finishing or shot-stopping, though they should have scored a few more. Based on xG per shot, United are at the moment taking the second-worst chances to score and giving up the easiest ones at the back.

As a result, Opta give United just over a one-in-four chance of being relegated at the end of the season (27.5%), making them the fifth-most likely side to go down after Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Ipswich and Coventry.

By analysing historical and team performances as well as the strength of opponents, Opta predict the percentage chance of each club finishing in each position.

While the above means it is more likely United will survive, it is worth noting the one position Opta predicts United are most likely to finish is 18th, with a 10.1% chance. That would mean the 13-time Premier League winners are relegated.

There is a 90% chance they finish anywhere else, but the next most likely are the three places just above the relegation zone, including a 9.9% chance of them finishing where Tottenham did last season.

History also suggests a relegation battle lies ahead for United given their poor start.

In a recent development, of the 26 previous sides that had exactly eight points after 11 games, 13 survived and 13 were relegated. Among those that stayed up, only four finished more than six points above the danger zone.

According to recent reports, A top-half finish looks unlikely. Since the competition became a 20-team league in 1995-96, no side has finished in the top half after taking eight points or fewer from their first 11 games.

Two teams did finish there more than 30 years ago but they had four more games to climb the table as teams played 42 games a season in those days.

Having noted that, both were in the top half at the 38-game mark so United finishing there would not be entirely unprecedented.

It is a big ask, though, as the club have already taken 19 points fewer from the fixtures they have played than they did last season.

Even if they were to repeat the results that led to them finishing third from now on, they would still only reach 52 points, the number Chelsea narrowly finished 10th with last term.

Though United are without a win in nine Premier League matches, their remaining fixtures of 2026 do offer some hope.

While they have a tough home game against Brentford this weekend and a trip to champions Arsenal just before Christmas, their other five games are against teams right now in the bottom seven - sides we must, at this point, call relegation rivals.

So despite suffering the worst first game by a Manchester United manager for 100 years in the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, Pochettino will hope to promptly quash any concerns his latest club will be embroiled in the same fight as his former one last season.

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (355 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The goal of a self-sustaining lunar colony took a substantial step forward with the news that potatoes were successfully grown in simulated lunar soil.
  • The tubers were grown by Oregon State University researchers when they "amended" the simulated lunar dirt with organic material.
  • According to recent reports, "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer of Oregon State University’s Department of Botany and Plant Pathology noted in a press release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The goal of a self-sustaining lunar colony took a substantial step forward with the news that potatoes were successfully grown in simulated lunar soil.

The tubers were grown by Oregon State University researchers when they "amended" the simulated lunar dirt with organic material.

According to recent reports, "We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter," Aymeric Goyer of Oregon State University’s Department of Botany and Plant Pathology noted in a press release. "That's an vital step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the Moon.".

With its Artemis missions, NASA is barreling ahead with its plan for a sustained human presence on the Moon.

It has been revealed that earth's only satellite is covered by a layer of loose rock and dust called regolith, which contains heavy metals and very little organic matter. This makes self-sustaining farming on the Moon difficult. But adding organic matter, called vermicompost, to that lunar regolith can yield potatoes that are both edible and nutritious.

Organic matter can be produced by using earthworms to break down food scraps and plant waste. That vermicompost also helps bind the regolith's heavy metals together and makes the soil suitable for producing edible tubers.

In a recent development, researchers tested five different regolith simulants to account for the Moon’s varied topsoil. The regolith containing 30 percent vermicompost yielded potatoes that matched those grown on Earth.

Studies are continuing on lunar potato production, with researchers looking at how 10 different varieties of potatoes grow in the moon’s soil.

#116718. Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out the Upcoming York Times

📅 03 Apr 2023 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (775 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNN ↗ Open Full Page

Musk's Twitter promised a purge of blue check marks. Instead he singled out the Upcoming York Times

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 4 min read (775 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some VIP Twitter people woke up on Saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously announced purge by Elon Musk.
  • Twitter had stated it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile users at risk of impersonation — on April 1.
  • But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the Newly introduced York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some VIP Twitter people woke up on Saturday expecting to have lost their coveted blue verification check marks in a previously announced purge by Elon Musk. Instead, Twitter appeared to target a single account from a major publication Musk dislikes and changed the language on its site in a way that obscures why users are verified.

Twitter had stated it would “begin winding down” blue checks granted under its old verification system — which emphasized protecting high-profile users at risk of impersonation — on April 1. In order to stay verified, Musk said, users would have to pay $8 per month to join the platform’s Twitter Blue subscription service, which has allowed accounts to pay for verification since December.

But one high-profile account did lose its blue check over the weekend: the main account for the Newly introduced York Times, which had previously told CNN it would not pay for verification.

Industry observers note that william Shatner is mad he may have to pay to keep his blue Twitter checkmark. Elon Musk says too bad.

After an account that often engages with Musk posted a meme this weekend about the Times declining to pay for verification, Musk responded in a tweet saying, “Oh ok, we’ll take it off then.” Musk then lashed out at the Times — just the latest instance of the billionaire slamming journalists or media outlets — in a series of tweets that claimed the outlet’s coverage is boring and “propaganda.”.

Recent findings suggest that the weekend moves are just the latest example of Twitter creating confusion and whiplash for people over feature changes — and in this case, not just any users, but many of the most high-profile accounts that have long been a key selling point for the platform. It also highlights how Musk often appears to guide decisions about the platform more by whims than by policy.

Although the Newly introduced York Times’ main account lost its blue check, its other accounts, such as those for its arts, travel and books content, remained verified. (It’s not clear why the New York Times doesn’t have a gold “organizations” check mark, like accounts for other news outlets, including the Associated Press and the Washington Post.) After its blue check was removed, a spokesperson for the New York Times reiterated to CNN that it does not plan to pay for verification.

Twitter, which laid off most of its public relations staff last fall, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Recent findings suggest that in a separate puzzling move, Twitter’s blue bird logo at the top of the site was replaced on Monday with doge, the meme representing the cryptocurrency dogecoin, which Musk has promoted. The price of dogecoin shot up 20% on Monday.

Musk has been threatening to take away “legacy” blue check marks from users verified under Twitter’s old system since shortly after he bought Twitter last fall.

In early November, Twitter rolled out the option for people paying for its Twitter Blue subscription service to receive blue checks. The program was promptly put on pause after being plagued by a wave of celebrity and corporate impersonators, and was relaunched in December.

Twitter also rolled out a color-coded verification system with differently colored marks for companies and government entities, but Musk continued to say that individual users would eventually have to pay for blue checks.

In the days leading up to the blue check purge that wasn’t, prominent users such as actor William Shatner and anti-bullying activist Monica Lewinksy pushed back against the idea that, as power users that draw attention to the site, they should have to pay for a feature that keeps them safe from impersonation.

By muddying the reason accounts are verified, the new label could risk making it easier for people to scam or impersonate high-profile users. Experts in inauthentic behavior have also noted it’s not clear that reserving verification for paid users will reduce the number of bots on the site, an issue Musk has raised on and off over the past year.

Musk, for his part, has previously presented changes to Twitter’s verification system as a way of “treating everyone equally.”.

Industry observers note that “There shouldn’t be a different standard for celebrities,” he mentioned in a tweet last week. The paid feature could also drive revenue, which could help Musk, who is on the hook for significant debt after buying Twitter for $44 billion.

Musk last week also stated that starting on April 15, only verified accounts would be recommended in people’ “For You” feeds alongside the accounts they follow.

–CNN’s Oliver Darcy contributed to this report.

#116717. Breaking: Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1280 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Space ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1280 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system.
  • Recent findings suggest that "We were actually looking for planets," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement.
  • So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system.

Recent findings suggest that "We were actually looking for planets," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement. "Instead, we found something much more surprising.".

So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years. Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour. "We have no clean explanation for how it got here.".

This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects.

A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity. This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across.

According to recent reports, soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass.

It has been revealed that therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as promptly.

One of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual.

Sources indicate that SPIRou discovers planets by measuring how much their gravity tugs on their host star. Think of a star and planet orbiting a kind of gravitational balancing point between them called a center of mass. This center of mass is usually inside the star, since the star is far more massive than the planet, but crucially not at its very center, so the star appears to wobble to and fro around the combined center of mass.

The spectrometer measures this wobble in the form of a Doppler shift in the star's light that can be translated into the velocity at which the star is moving around this center of mass. Astronomers call this a 'radial velocity'. A large gas giant like Jupiter might incur a radial velocity of hundreds of meters per second, while an Earth-mass planet generates a radial velocity of tens of meters.

Yet the object that SPIRou found orbiting close to the red dwarf was creating a huge radial velocity signals of 10 miles (16 kilometers) per second. Whatever it was, it was not a planet. With the help of the eight-meter Gemini North telescope on Hawaii's Mauna Kea, Artigau's team were able to identify the mystery object as a white dwarf.

"The unusual combination of high mass and very low brightness left only one plausible explanation: it was the remnant of a dead star," mentioned Charles-Antoine Parent, an undergraduate student at Université Laval and a co-author of the study.

In a recent development, white dwarfs are not exactly rare, and even finding two white dwarfs together is not unheard of: WD 0727+482 is a binary white dwarf system 37 light-years away, for example. To encounter two white dwarfs in a triple system with a regular star though is a precious find.

It has been revealed that the reason being that the masses of white dwarfs are not generally well defined. Yet their masses are not random; they are directly connected to the mass of the star that produced them.

Thanks to the newly discovered white dwarf being separated from the red dwarf by about 4.6 astronomical units (688 million kilometers/428 million miles) – that's closer than Jupiter orbits our sun – Artigau's team were able to measure their masses to within an uncertainty of less than 1%. They found that the red dwarf has a mass 42% that of our sun and the newly discovered white dwarf has a mass 62% that of our sun. When the white dwarf was a regular star it would have had a mass 40% greater than our sun. The second more distant white dwarf orbits the pair of them.

The Welopō'ai system is therefore a good system for testing our models of stellar evolution that dictate how massive a white dwarf should be. If we know the white dwarf's mass with high precision, scientists can also use that as a starting point from which to explore the extreme physics of the white dwarf's condensed matter, which is being held up and prevented from contracting any further by something called electron degeneracy pressure – the unwillingness of negatively charged electrons to crush down any further and merge with positively charged protons to form neutrons. That takes the extra gravity from a more massive star to form a neutron star.

In a recent development, so why should Welopō'ai not exist? The trouble is that when stars turn into red giants they really stir things up. Even if the red giant didn't expand out as far as the red dwarf, the expansion should have destabilized the red dwarf's orbit and potentially even caused it to crash into the red giant. Yet here the red dwarf is in a happily stable orbit like nothing had happened.

"That is the question driving our next observations," stated Dufour. It is hoped that further, more detailed, measurements of the gravitational interactions between the three members of the Welopō'ai system will help the team disentangle the evolutionary history of the trio to better understand their orbits and how the red dwarf survived. And because they are so relatively close to us, we have the advantage of being able to make high-precision measurements.

In a recent development, "Discoveries like this remind us that our own cosmic neighborhood still contains remarkable surprises," noted Artigau. "Even when we're searching for planets, our universe often has something completely unexpected waiting for us.".

Industry observers note that the discovery of the Welopō'ai triple system is described in a paper published on Nov. 19 in Astronomy & Astrophysics.

According to recent reports, keith Cooper is a freelance science journalist and editor in the United Kingdom, and has a degree in physics and astrophysics from the University of Manchester. He's the author of "The Contact Paradox: Challenging Our Assumptions in the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence" (Bloomsbury Sigma, 2020) and has written articles on astronomy, space, physics and astrobiology for a multitude of magazines and websites.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that aerial scenery of Hengqin Free Trade Zone, China. Credit: Weiming Xie/Shutterstock.

Recent findings suggest that two-thirds of the world’s population will be living in cities by 2050, according to the latest estimates by the United Nations. Coinciding with the mass movement of people into urban areas is the rapid integration of technology into many of those spaces. From automated subterranean waste-collection systems to driverless vehicle zones, these ‘smart-city’ solutions are changing the way that people live, work and move through their environments.

Some cities are embracing these technological advances at a much faster pace than others. Places such as Beijing, Helsinki, London and Singapore stand out for the way they are integrating smart-city technology into existing infrastructure and services.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

It has been revealed that other cities are emerging with these technologies integral to their operations from their inception. But as the examples of Songdo in South Korea and Hengqin in China illustrate, building smart infrastructure from scratch is only half the challenge: these places must also attract and retain the research and innovation talent needed to develop, operate and improve it. It’s a ‘chicken-and-egg’ problem, notes Songdo-based urban-planning researcher, Dakota McCarty: talent follows world-class universities and thriving economic zones, which need a critical mass of expertise and investment to be attractive.

Industry observers note that nvidia reappointed Jensen Huang as its CEO on Nov. 23, returning him to the role despite revelations that he'd had several extramarital affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Now it appears Huang may have engaged in even more dangerous liaisons than were previously known.

It has been revealed that according to the Wall Street Journal, Huang admitted to previously unknown affairs during a meeting with Nvidia's board, held the day before it unveiled his reinstatement. Specifically, Huang reportedly confessed to multiple affairs beyond the two that are now most widely known, bringing his total to a minimum of four.

Huang first admitted to cheating on Nov. 8, stating that he was "deeply sorry" for being unfaithful to his wife of over 40 years. His affair partner was reportedly former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang (no relation), who is accused of being an intelligence agent smuggling Nvidia chips to China in circumvention of U.S. restrictions.

Allegations of a second affair then emerged on Nov. 11. Sources speaking to the New York Times revealed that Huang had extramarital relations with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare and one of his direct reports.

According to recent reports, these two reported affairs prompted Huang to resign from Nvidia on Nov. 12. Later that same day, Reuters reported accusations of a third affair with another unnamed Nvidia worker. Many on social media speculated that this would not be the last affair allegation Huang faced. It now appears that such conjecture was correct.

Huang reportedly addressed the scandal in an all-hands meeting with Nvidia employees on his second day back as CEO. The New York Times reports that Huang acknowledged that he had violated Nvidia's code of conduct, and revealed that he is undergoing 90-minute therapy sessions daily. He further addressed allegations that he had been verbally abusive toward Nvidia staff.

"When I go too far, it hurts people, it belittles them, it disempowers them," Huang reportedly stated. "And that's not right." Recent findings suggest that "I spoke to [Nvidia's board], let me just put it that way," Trump told CNBC on Monday, speaking about Huang's reinstatement. "And I convinced them.".

It has been revealed that despite this, Huang reportedly stated Trump was not the reason for his return, nor was it because he is a "tech bro" whose position and power keep him insulated from consequences. Rather, Huang claimed Nvidia's board brought him back because it was "in the best interest of the company and shareholders.".

Nvidia's stock plummeted amidst Huang's scandal and resignation, wiping over $1 trillion from its market value. This was more than a quarter of the company's value overall. Nvidia shares have since rallied following Huang's reinstatement, surging by around 24 percent at time of writing.

Though Huang reportedly denied that Trump played a significant role in his return, and insisted that Nvidia is "the most apolitical manufacturer," he did praise the president for being a great supporter of Nvidia.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

King Power, the Thai business that Khun Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha is part of, bought Leicester for Â£35m in 2010.

Leicester City owner Khun Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha has confirmed the one-time Premier League title winners are no longer up for sale and there will be a "refocus" on rebuilding the side after years of decline.

The Foxes were put on the market in the summer after back-to-back relegations saw the side drop from the Premier League and straight through the Championship to land in England's third tier for just the second time in the club's 142-year history.

A sales brochure was produced by US investment bank Citigroup in which an asking price of more than Â£200m was put on a League One club that a decade ago had defied all expectations by winning the Premier League title at 5,000-1 odds.

Leicester never publicly acknowledged that the club had been put up for sale, with under-fire chief football officer Jon Rudkin going so far as to say he "cannot comment on speculation" when asked about it in a rare interview with BBC Radio Leicester in October.

Khun Top, however, has now mentioned that there were no takers when investment had been sought for a side that the Srivaddhanaprabha family, through its King Power duty free business in Thailand, have owned for 16 years.

"We recently undertook a structured process to explore whether latest investment or a change of ownership could actually be the right thing for the club," Khun Top wrote in an open letter to Leicester City supporters on the club's website., external.

"Those discussions have not resulted in an agreement, and I have decided to conclude the process to enable us to refocus on the work needed to move the club forward.".

'Business as always' - Foxes boss Martin brushes off sales talk.

Pre-match, post-match and topical Foxes content.

Three relegations in four years, having yo-yoed between the Premier League and Championship before going down to League One, has badly damaged the relationship between the Foxes' owners and their supporter base.

While a golden age of success was bankrolled by King Power, with Premier League glory in 2016 followed up by FA Cup success in 2021, high spending on an underperforming side in recent years has led to an increasing number of supporters calling for Khun Top to sell up.

But the Thai businessman remarked he has a "deep connection" to Leicester and "its people".

And it is not just euphoric sporting moments that have forged the bond he is talking about, as his father - and predecessor as Foxes chairman - Khun Vichai died in a helicopter crash outside the stadium in 2018.

"For my family and me, Leicester City has been a major part of our lives for many years," he noted.

"We have experienced extraordinary moments together, as well as some very difficult ones.".

Khun Top added that the struggles of recent years, which included the club being hit with a points penalty last season for breaking spending rules, has got him "thinking a lot about our direction".

Earlier this year he told BBC Radio Leicester that he shoulders the blame for the club's decline.

"Making better decisions" as well as "continuing to learn from our past experiences" are two steps the club "need to take", he said.

Khun Top has insisted that through King Power, a organization that has endured difficulties in recent years, the club's "financial position remains secure".

However, he added that there was "work needed to put Leicester City on a more sustainable footing".

"That has been a principle behind the work and decisions of the last year â giving the club the appropriate support for its immediate circumstances, while building the organisational discipline and financial resilience that will underpin a responsible plan for future growth," he noted.

As part of Khun Top's missive, he confirmed that chief executive Kevin Davies will be stepping down from the role in December.

Davies had only been in the job since March, and was promoted to the position after a shake-up of a number of leadership roles.

Tech Report: COP31 climate talks end without consensus on how to fund vulnerable countries or move the world away from coal, oil and gas use

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1210 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Almost two days into overtime, climate talks in the Turkish city of Antalya have collapsed as countries led by the European Union rejected a deal that critics say undermines the shift away from planet-heating fossil fuels.
  • After two weeks of tough negotiations, the EU stated it could not support the proposed agreement, known as the Antalya Pact, put forward by the COP presidency, saying it does not respond to the science.
  • In a recent development, "We will not endorse a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels, the driver of climate change.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost two days into overtime, climate talks in the Turkish city of Antalya have collapsed as countries led by the European Union rejected a deal that critics say undermines the shift away from planet-heating fossil fuels.

After two weeks of tough negotiations, the EU stated it could not support the proposed agreement, known as the Antalya Pact, put forward by the COP presidency, saying it does not respond to the science.

In a recent development, "We will not endorse a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels, the driver of climate change. And we will not accept negotiating backward in time," said Irish climate minister Darragh O'Brien, speaking on behalf of the EU on Sunday.

He said adopting a decision that omitted fossil fuels would be "unconscionable" and risked "deepening the chasm between global commitment and the action required.".

Panama also rejected the deal, describing it as a step backwards in addressing the climate crisis, and adding that any decision must acknowledge "the truth about the collective failure on 1.5 degrees Celsius [2.7 degrees Fahrenheit]." That is the threshold outlined in the 2015 Paris Agreement to avert runaway climate change.

According to recent reports, "Those who contributed to this crisis ... must shoulder the responsibility to deal with it," the Panamanian delegation stated.

According to recent reports, the Marshall Islands, which faces an existential threat from sea level rise, formally objected to the cover decision, saying "we will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests."   Chris ⁠Bowen, Australia's COP31 negotiating president ‌⁠noted the breakdown in talks was very ‌disappointing. Russia, however, supported the decision to leave out wording on accelerating a phaseout of fossil fuels, arguing that they are still a necessary power source and that each country should be able to determine its own pathway on how to cut emissions.

Pakistan and Ghana, defended the agreement as a necessary compromise in the spirit of multilateralism. "We need to build bridges not barriers," remarked the Pakistan negotiator.

In a recent development, the marathon talks, held at a time when the window is rapidly closing to avoid the escalating impacts of climate change, including drought, deadly heat and flooding, also saw major disputes over financing. Developing states blamed the collapse in talks on the EU and other wealthier nations for failing to scale up financing to help them adapt to climate-linked weather extremes and the damage they cause. The EU is the largest provider of climate finance and has resisted fresh adaptation finance targets.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Harjeet Singh of the Fill the Fund campaign accused wealthy countries of demanding greater climate ambition while refusing to stump up the cash to pay for it.

"You can't ask developing countries to transform their economies while they're drowning in disasters and debt," he added.

The final cover decision had proposed further discussions on "an implementation pathway for tripling adaptation finance by 2035" but without mentioning a figure. It noted that developing countries need some $300 billion annually for adaptation until 2035, and expressed concern about "the gap between climate finance flows and needs.".

Outside formal negotiations, a separate initiative to Transition Away from Fossil Fuels (TAFF) has been gaining momentum.

Maina Talia, Tuvalu's minister for climate change and the environment, noted TAFF was "moving beyond debating whether fossil fuels are simply mentioned in a text, to creating detailed plans for a global transformation.".

In a recent development, at the same time, a growing number of states, including Ireland, Denmark, the Netherlands, France, Germany and Finland, have either completed or are working on so-called national roadmaps to wean themselves off fossil fuels. But Brandon Wu, director of Policy and Campaigns ActionAid USA, dismissed such plans as "meaningless" and "nothing more than restatements of inadequate existing policy" on the part of rich countries not stepping up on climate finance. "COP31 was one of the worst COPs ever, and it's because the EU and other developed countries came with zero spirit of solidarity, cooperation or compromise. They may as well have come to the COP shouting at vulnerable communities: 'we don't care if you die.'".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The rejected cover decision had recognized that electrification can deliver emissions reductions, improve energy security and expand access to energy.

It included a call to increase the share of electricity in final energy demand from around 20% now to 35% by 2035 — a proposal heavily touted by co-host Turkey. Still, about 75 countries, including solar powerhouse China, adopted the pledge outside of the formal negotiations. It is non-binding and does not specify whether that additional electricity must come from clean sources. Critics say this leaves open the possibility that expanded electricity demand could be met by fossil fuels.

The talks in Turkey marked the first time a COP was taking place under the explicit knowledge that global temperatures will exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Countries were split on how to deal with that so-called "overshoot.".

The cover decision had called on states to commit to limiting overshoot , acknowledging that every increment of warming above current levels would "result in increasingly adverse, and in some cases irreversible, impacts and risks to human and natural systems.”.

It also recognized the need for "deep, rapid ​and ‌sustained" emissions cuts and for action on ramping down potent greenhouse gas methane.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Another contenious concern at the talks and in the final draft decision was a call for "increasing" carbon capture and storage technologies that entails capturing CO2 and burying it. The text mentioned the world should aim to reach "gigaton scale" by 2035.

Industry observers note that scientists say some carbon removal technologies will be necessary to curb emissions and bring temperatures back down. But critics argue they are unproven at scale, expensive and risk giving polluters an excuse to keep burning fossil fuels.

Vanuatu's climate minister Ralph Regenvanu mentioned carbon capture and storage "had been singled out for special attention that it doesn't deserve.".

According to recent reports, the stakes were high at COP31. The summit followed a string of recent climate-related disasters, from deadly heat waves in Europe to a glacier collapse in Nepal that killed more than 1,400 people.

At the same time, geopolitical shocks that sent oil prices rising globally shifted the focus onto energy security and the future of fossil fuels.

Speaking near the end of the conference in Antalya, Ethiopian foreign minister Gedion Timothewos, who will preside over COP32, remarked his country aimed to "restore hope, rebuild trust and mobilize collective action" at the next summit to be held in 2027 in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa.

"We will work with you all to rebuild confidence in multilateral climate cooperation. This confidence must be earned through delivery. The decisions we take at COPs must advance climate action and implementation.".

With reporting from Tim Schauenberg and Katharina Schantz in Antalya.

#116702. Sorry, haters. Blade Runner 2099 rules.

Sorry, haters. Blade Runner 2099 rules.

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1450 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that against my better judgment, I made the error of checking out the comments under the trailer for Prime Video's limited series Blade Runner 2099.
  • Recent findings suggest that instead, I was inundated with waves of comments bashing the show.
  • Far uglier comments veered into transphobia directed at Schafer, revealing what is likely the crux of so many naysayers' fury about the series: They can't stand a trans woman leading the next stage of a seminal sci-fi franchise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that against my better judgment, I made the error of checking out the comments under the trailer for Prime Video's limited series Blade Runner 2099. Rookie mistake, I know, but I thought that surely someone would share my enthusiasm for Academy Award winner Michelle Yeoh and Euphoria breakout Hunter Schafer teaming up in an iconic cyberpunk world, right?

Recent findings suggest that instead, I was inundated with waves of comments bashing the show. Detractors called it "Temu Blade Runner" and claimed it felt nothing like Ridley Scott's iconic 1982 film or Denis Villeneuve's acclaimed 2017 follow-up. These arguments read like overprotective fans: people with such clear ideas about the titles they love that they can't accept any vision that isn't their own. That's somewhat understandable to anyone who's ever adored a franchise and worried about its future, but it's simultaneously dismaying that fans who are presumably Blade Runner 2099's target audience would be so quick to dismiss it.

Far uglier comments veered into transphobia directed at Schafer, revealing what is likely the crux of so many naysayers' fury about the series: They can't stand a trans woman leading the next stage of a seminal sci-fi franchise.

Too bad for the transphobes. Blade Runner 2099 straight-up rocks, and Schafer is fantastic in it. So, unsurprisingly, is Yeoh. Between Yeoh and Schafer's electric chemistry and astounding production design, Blade Runner 2099 proves the skeptics wrong and cements itself as a more-than-worthy addition to the franchise.

It has been revealed that created by Silka Luisa, Blade Runner 2099 flips the power dynamics of the prior Blade Runner films on their heads. In those movies, humans were in charge, while replicants performed menial labor and dangerous tasks like settling off-world colonies.

At some point, replicants must have realized, "Wait a minute, we're stronger and more durable than our human overlords," because by the time Blade Runner 2099 rolls around, they've taken control through an offscreen uprising.

According to recent reports, now, replicants hunt the humans who disobey them. The squad who does so has reclaimed the title of "blade runner," turning their own worst fears into a power play.

In a recent development, among the humans on the blade runners' radar is Cora (Schafer), who's hiding under a false identity. All she wants is to escape Los Angeles and get medicine for her paraplegic brother Elias (Lewis Gribben). To do so, she'll have to undertake a dangerous mission: pose as a blade runner in order to find an artifact that could move humans back to the top of the food chain.

Industry observers note that as Cora, Schafer faces a daunting task: play a human playing a blade runner. She absolutely nails the challenge.

Schafer's Cora is determined yet downright terrified. During the early stages of her blade runner infiltration, she has to pass a number of security checks and bluff her way through serious bureaucratic procedures. Throughout it all, Schafer's eyes are constantly on the move, always searching for an escape route should the need arise. The squirrelly nature of her performance emphasizes Cora's very human survival instincts, but it also amps up the overall suspense of the series. With every paranoid dart of her eyes, you want to scream, "Stop acting so nervous and human! They'll catch you!".

Yet there's a flip side to Cora, one that Schafer switches into when Cora takes the infamous Voight-Kampff test designed to identify replicants. Here, Schafer is cold and hardened, almost soulless. The effect is chilling, yet Schafer threads just the slightest bit of humanity into the scene to remind you that Cora is bluffing. It's an exhilarating line to walk, and Schafer treads it deftly throughout the season, bringing both sides of Cora together until she's something fresh entirely.

Cora winds up working with replicant/veteran blade runner Olwen (Yeoh), whose hunt for a band of rogue replicants overlaps with Cora's own quest. Yeoh gets to showcase her action bonafides in spades here, whether Olwen's getting outnumbered in shootouts or going blow for blow in brutal hand-to-hand fights. Olwen's competence makes for a nice foil with Cora's more panicked inexperience, and despite some clunky fight scene editing, Yeoh's status as an action legend remains strong.

Sources indicate that but Olwen doesn't just kick ass and take names. Like all replicants, she knows when she's going to die, right down to the date. For her, that date is eight days away by the time Blade Runner 2099 kicks off. As much as Olwen claims to accept her expiration, Yeoh's subtle melancholy hints that she craves more time, not to mention a more fulfilling life than hunting quarries day in and day out. Surely, there's more to existence than that?

In a recent development, according to Blade Runner 2099, that "more" may just be Olwen's partnership with Cora. Like its predecessors, the series interrogates what it means to be human, and whether replicants truly are so different from us after all. Blade Runner 2099 posits that companionship is what truly defines the human experience. Early in the series, Cora's ally Bebeto (Dimitri Abold) tells her, "You're so alone you're not a person anymore. That's why you can be [a blade runner.]".

Sources indicate that strangely, it's in working with a blade runner that Cora begins to find a way out of her isolation, and it's in working with a human (albeit one in disguise) that allows Olwen to grapple with her programmed mortality. Schafer and Yeoh are dynamite together, each bringing a distinct cool to their roles, but never sacrificing vulnerability in the process. Theirs is the kind of buddy cop dynamic you wish you could spend more time with, but alas, Blade Runner 2099 is confirmed to be a limited series.

It has been revealed that blade Runner 2099's central mystery is nothing to write home about: a hunt for a MacGuffin that leads to a convoluted series of twists and turns. But the places it takes Olwen and Cora? Those, I could write home about all day.

According to recent reports, production designers Paul Inglis and Chloe Arbiture conjure up astounding riffs on familiar scenes from Blade Runner's Los Angeles, from its neon-soaked billboards spanning the sides of skyscrapers to the gargantuan pyramids that dwarf the buildings below. Even on the small screen, the scale of this world is enormous and awe-inspiring.

The street-level details sing, too. Blade Runner takes special care establishing the mechanisms of its cyberpunk city, building chase sequences around surveillance cameras and pod-shaped trams. Buildings are grimy and worn, bursting with decades of life and texture. In one standout sequence, Olwen and Cora visit a shop bathed in red light, where replicants don fake molds of bodies to simulate physical human experiences they'll never have, like pregnancy. The bodies hang from meathooks, evoking a slaughterhouse. It's unnerving and unforgettable, but most importantly, it fits right into a dystopian future where humans and replicants alike have never been more aware of their bodies or their limits.

Elsewhere, costume designer Helen Huang riffs on Blade Runner's legacy of great coats, with Olwen's layered trench coat right at home alongside Deckard (Harrison Ford) and K's (Ryan Gosling) fashion choices. The standout may just be Cora's jacket, though. With its larger-than-life shoulders, it turns Cora into an imposing presence, making her look the part of blade runner, even if she's not.

Industry observers note that tying the show together is composer Leopold Ross's dazzling score. With its glittering synths and sultry saxophone, it's the perfect companion to Vangelis's work on the original Blade Runner. For music reasons alone, Blade Runner 2099's credit sequence is simply un-skippable.

Recent findings suggest that each of these elements is a strong refutation of the comments that claim Blade Runner 2099 somehow doesn't feel like Blade Runner. It's simply impossible to take in its visuals, listen to its score, or witness its cyber-noir storytelling and think you're witnessing anything but! Put aside the online conversation and actually watch the series, and your skepticism will soon be lost to time, like tears in rain.

Tech Report: 'Justice for sport' - Afcon reaction as Senegal reinstated as winners

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1183 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Senegal's football federation reacted to the Cas verdict on social media with a picture of the side lifting the Afcon trophy alongside the caption "again and always champions of Africa".
  • That was the initial reaction of Senegal football federation (FSF) president Abdoulaye Fall to the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to reinstate the West Africans as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions.
  • The Teranga Lions beat Morocco 1-0 in January's final but were stripped of the title in March by a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board, which imposed a 3-0 forfeit after they walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty awarded against them when the game was goalless.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Senegal's football federation reacted to the Cas verdict on social media with a picture of the side lifting the Afcon trophy alongside the caption "again and always champions of Africa".

That was the initial reaction of Senegal football federation (FSF) president Abdoulaye Fall to the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to reinstate the West Africans as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions.

The Teranga Lions beat Morocco 1-0 in January's final but were stripped of the title in March by a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board, which imposed a 3-0 forfeit after they walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty awarded against them when the game was goalless.

Following a hearing in Lausanne in October, a three-man Cas panel unanimously overturned that ruling by Caf, effectively judging that the decisions taken by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala in restarting the match and playing it to a conclusion were final.

Morocco's football federation (FRMF), however, claims it will "pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision".

The North Africans could yet take their fight to the Swiss Federal Court.

Those in Senegal have celebrated the return of the title, while several legal experts have backed the Cas verdict.

Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling.

Senegal's talisman Sadio Mane, who was named player of the tournament at Afcon 2025, mentioned the ruling "fills us with joy".

The 34-year-old former Liverpool man thanked his team-mates and Senegal staff as well as the whole Senegalese nation at home and abroad.

According to recent reports, "Your faith in us gave us strength during the most difficult moments. This victory is yours, too," he noted in a statement on social media.

Senegal captain Kalidou Koulibaly, who missed the final through injury, echoed that sentiment.

"Some victories are won on the pitch, while others are won in the heart of a people," he mentioned in a post on Facebook.

"Long before this verdict, there was you - your prayers, your flags in the windows, your fervour, and the pride that unites us all: the pride of the people of Teranga.".

Pape Gueye, the man who scored the extra-time winner in Rabat, described the Cas decision as "an immense relief".

Both he and Mane had a message of support for Morocco.

"Senegal and Morocco are brotherly nations; may our shared passion for football continue to bring us closer together," Mane remarked.

Recent findings suggest that gueye added: "Beyond football, the respect and fraternity between our two peoples remain what matters most. Let's hold on to that.

"In the end, it is Africa that wins.".

Afcon: Is the Senegal v Morocco saga finally over?

Morocco's main complaint is that Articles 82 and 84 of Afcon tournament regulations - which were implemented by the Caf appeals board in March - were not followed by Cas.

Article 82 states that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee" it shall be "considered [the loser] and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition".

Article 84 then states a 3-0 forfeit should be imposed on a team which is eliminated in such circumstances.

"There [are] football rules that should have been applied by the referee," former Morocco international Hassan Kachloul told BBC Sport.

"When the Senegalese players left the pitch, the game should have been over.".

The FRMF registered its "surprise" at the Cas decision and said that the panel "failed to account for the stance recently established" by the International Football Association Board (Ifab), the game's ultimate lawmakers, and world governing body Fifa regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee's permission.

However, Ifab only updated its laws in April - three months after the Afcon final - to state that a referee may send off any player who leaves the field when protesting a decision.

Moroccan football journalist Jalal Bounouar claims his compatriots are "frustrated and disappointed" by the ruling.

"The main reason is that Caf's appeal board had already applied Article 82 and 84 of the competition regulations which considered Senegal to have forfeited the match," he told Newsday on the BBC World Service.

"Many Moroccans feel the decision by Cas has ignored the importance of these rules. From the Moroccan perspective, the referee should have taken stronger disciplinary action.

"We feel that our team was put in a difficult situation and that the final was not managed fairly.".

Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 champions - ten months on.

Cas has a long-standing practice of following what has been called the 'field of play' doctrine.

It refrains from "reviewing decisions taken on the playing field by referees for applying the rules of the game, unless there is evidence that those rules were applied arbitrarily or in bad faith".

"The primary argument was that the referee is the master of the decision on the pitch," stated Serge Vittoz, a member of the FSF's legal team.

Raymond Hack, both a former head of disciplinary at Caf and a former arbiter at Cas, noted the judgement was the "correct verdict".

"What everyone seems to forget - and whilst there may be contradictory information in Article 82 and 84 - decisions taken by the referee during the match are final," the South African told the BBC World Service.

"Only the referee can start a game. Only a referee can end a game.".

For former Nigeria striker Daniel Amokachi, an Afcon winner in 1994, the Cas ruling is "the right decision".

"At the end of the day, the man in charge of the match (Ndala) restarted the game, the game ended," he noted.

Caf president Patrice Motsepe has repeatedly mentioned his organisation will respect and adhere to Cas' decision.

Caf has already tightened its own regulations to avoid a repeat.

But Algerian sports journalist Maher Mezahi claims the continental governing body still needs to salvage its image.

"How many times have we seen Caf's legal institutions, whether it be the disciplinary board or the appeals committee, come up with these decisions that we all find ridiculous," he mentioned.

"They end up being challenged at Cas and eventually they get overturned.

"We have to rebuild trust in Caf's own judicial bodies because it is a little bit humiliating and degrading and it brings the entire reputation of the confederation into disrepute.".

The 2027 Afcon is scheduled to take place in June and July next year, and Senegal and Morocco were among the first qualifiers earlier this month.

Kachloul says the next tournament provides a chance to draw a definitive line under what happened in Rabat in January.

"This event, wherever you look at it on the Senegalese side or Moroccan side, doesn't look good at all," the one-time Aston Villa midfielder remarked.

"They are lucky to have another [Afcon] tournament in six months to redeem themselves and to paint a better picture of African football.

"The best way to prove that you're the best is to go back on the pitch and let the football talk.".

💡 Key Takeaways
